title: Germany's Fragile Recovery Tests Merz's Pro-Growth Agenda · 26 Aug
keywords: Germany, economy, GDP, recovery, Friedrich Merz, reform, inflation, Ifo index, ZEW, eurozone, labour market, fiscal policy, competitiveness, structural reform, European Union
notes: Germany's economy grew 0.3% in the second quarter of 2026, lifting business and investor sentiment and prompting the government to argue that a durable recovery is underway. But critics warn that modest growth, persistent inflation, and deep structural weaknesses mean the country is not yet out of the woods. Chancellor Friedrich Merz is pressing ahead with a reform agenda aimed at restoring competitiveness, even as opponents question whether ordinary Germans will feel the benefits soon enough.
